messages:
alex_rm: Hey team — customer ACME reported a sudden spike of 401s for /v1/generate after midnight UTC. They say it coincided with a key rotation on their IdP. Error in logs: "invalid_signature". Raising here before we open a formal SEV. Ticket AC-8342.

mira_sec: thanks Alex. can you paste the exact error payload and the incoming JWT header? often we see kid aliasing or jwks cache TTL issues.

alex_rm: pasted from their support dump:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_signature",
  "detail": "signature verification failed (kid: 'alpha-2026-03-15')"
}
```

They also sent the header: `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"alpha-2026-03-15"}`

Their JWKS endpoint returns both old+new keys for a short window. They said they rotated keys at 00:05 UTC and started seeing errors ~00:07. They claim their client sent a freshly-signed token after rotation.

jonah_rt: possible causes: our JWKS cache hasn't refreshed yet and we still used the old public key; or kid mismatch if they reused kids across rotations; or clock skew causing token to be considered not-yet-valid if nbf/iat drift. what's our jwks cache TTL for hosted API right now?

mira_sec: TTL is 5m by default for external JWKS fetch, with background refresh at half the TTL. we also have a fallback path that fetches on signature fail if the kid isn't present, but I think that only kicks if kid not found — not if key present but signature doesn't match because keys are semantically different.

priya_oncall: oncall here — can we repro quickly? alex, do we have the raw token or headers to replay? if not, ask customer for an obfuscated token (keep first/last chars) so we can try verifying against our JWKS snapshot vs fresh fetch.

alex_rm: requested token. they gave a redacted token: `eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImFscGhhLTIwMjYtMDMtMTUifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJj...`

sam_sre: a few operational notes: last JWKS fetch to their IdP from our edge was at 00:03 UTC (edge logs show 00:03:22) and next background refresh scheduled 00:08:22. so at 00:07 when the customer sent new token, our edge hadn't refreshed yet. fallback would help if kid missing, but here kid matches an entry in the cached JWKS — but that key corresponds to the old public key (different modulus) so verification fails.

mira_sec: that's interesting: kid present but signature mismatch. two immediate mitigations: 1) on signature verification failure, if kid present, trigger an immediate JWKS refresh and retry verification once (fast-path). 2) add short skew-tolerant window for accepted signatures if possible (but that helps only for time claims). option 1 is more straightforward.

jonah_rt: we already have logic to fetch JWKS on kid-not-found. expanding it to also fetch on signature-fail seems reasonable but watch for amplification/latency if an attacker triggers repeated failed sigs. need rate-limiting per issuer/kid and circuit-breaker.

priya_oncall: agreed — add per-issuer backoff and max retries 1 per request. Also log the attempted remote fetch and mark the edge as "stale-jwks" metric to alert. I'll take on the metric.

alex_rm: customer asked if clock skew could be the cause. their system clocks are within ±30s of NTP. token iat/nbf are fine. their failure logs show invalid_signature specifically, not exp/nbf. so likely key mismatch.

mira_sec: ok. plan: 1) short-term support playbook to send to ACME — ask them to: a) keep old key available for at least 5 minutes post-rotation, or b) change rotation to publish new kid first and keep old key in JWKS for fallback. we've seen clients with aggressive rotation windows fail. 2) infra change: implement immediate JWKS refresh-on-signature-fail with per-issuer rate-limit and a 1s retry window. 3) longer-term: implement verification that compares jwks.kid -> key fingerprint and emit an alert when the same kid maps to a different modulus (kid-reuse detection).

jonah_rt: for the patch: I'll add a conditional in verifier.js:

```
try {
  verify(token, cachedKey)
} catch (e) {
  if (e.name === 'JsonWebTokenError' && e.message.includes('invalid signature')) {
    if (!rateLimiter.allow(issuer)) throw e
    await jwksClient.refresh(issuer)
    const newKey = jwksClient.getKey(kid)
    return verify(token, newKey)
  }
  throw e
}
```

We'll instrument to count retry hits. keep retry count per-request at 1.

sam_sre: also ensure refresh uses a short-circuit: if we already had a fresh fetch in last 30s, skip. prevents thundering herd on rotation storms.

priya_oncall: I'll open an internal pagerable alert rule if we see >50 signature-fail->refresh cycles in 5m across edges. route to eng-security and SRE.

alex_rm: messaging to customer: ask them to confirm upcoming rotation times + provide best-effort replay token. tell them we're deploying a hotfix (refresh-on-failure) to prod edge in ~2 hours, and will follow up.

mira_sec: one more edgecase: some IdPs reuse kid strings across separate key families (they use deterministic kid based on metadata, not modulus). if we ever detect kid mapped to different 'alg' or different key type (RSA vs EC) between cached and fetched jwks, treat it as high-severity and require explicit operator approval before automatic acceptance. will add that check.

jonah_rt: estimate for hotfix: 2-3 dev hours + 30m canary + deploy. I'll queue a PR and add unit tests for: (a) signature-fail triggers refresh and verification succeeds with new key, (b) rate-limit prevents repeated fetches.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/hotfix/jwks-refresh-on-failure -> canary -> prod. PR #3421. ETA: 2h 15m. :rocket: 

alex_rm: thanks all — I'll send customer the short-term instructions and note we're rolling a fix. assigning to AC-8342 and SEV-eta if they escalate. :thumbsup:

mira_sec: follow-ups: I'll add a short runbook snippet for support: sample logs to collect, how to check edge jwks timestamp (`curl -s https://edge-log-api/internal/jwks?issuer=... | jq .last_fetch`). Also will add a one-liner they can run to verify:

```
# verify locally against fresh JWKS
curl -s https://example-issuer/.well-known/jwks.json | node verify_token.js 'eyJ...'
```

keep me posted if customer replays token and still fails.
